title: Albanian Principalities
capsule: The Albanian principalities were a constellation of medieval lordships that emerged across Albania and the western Balkans after the fragmentation of the Serbian Empire following Stefan Dušan's death in 1355. The most prominent figures included Karl Topia, who controlled central Albania and the Adriatic port of Durrës, and Gjon Kastrioti of the Principality of Kastrioti, whose son Gjergj (Skanderbeg) would forge the League of Lezhë in 1444 — a coalition that repelled Ottoman forces in more than twenty-eight engagements. Most individual principalities fell to Ottoman conquest between the 1390s and the 1420s; by 1422 the last independent lordships had been extinguished or reduced to vassalage.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extents of the individual principalities are only broadly reconstructable from narrative chronicles and diplomatic records; boundaries between overlapping Albanian, Serbian, and Ottoman spheres remain poorly documented.
